items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Joe Newman. If Basie was in town you use half the Basie band, and all these people became friends of yours, close friends, not just people that you would see on recording sessions, but guys you could hang out with and have a very nice life with.

ctx.x: What kind of sessions would those be? Were those jazz sessions?

Mostly jazz sessions. The first one I ever did which actually got me into a lot of hot water because of it, and they figured out I can always do this, was one for Al Cohn. I think the project was called “Mr. Music.” And I wrote a piece called “Cohn My Way.” And that came out of, I had remembered a little phrase that he played in one of his solos, and I used that and made a piece out of it on the way down. And that got the producer to start thinking about me when they were in trouble. I mean they wouldn’t think…

the love that you have between yourself and the players is what makes the whole thing work. If you can’t get your friends there, you’d better get some pretty good playing enemies, which I don’t think I have any. I love it. I come into a record session, I think I’m more relaxed than I have been for years and years, I think I’m more relaxed in a recording session than I am in my own living room half the time. Because you’re with 17, 18, 30 of your friends, and you expect the best out of them, and they are the best…
